message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling on Schluter-like profiles. Candidates are 7610.90 (aluminum structures and parts of structures), 7604.21 (hollow profiles), 7604.29 (other bars, rods, and profiles), and 7616.99 (other articles of aluminum).

The profiles are open (not hollow) and have punched holes, so they are worked beyond simple extrusion. Heading 7604 covers aluminum bars, rods, and profiles, and a profile that has been punched is still classified there unless it has been prepared for structural use. Heading 7610 covers structures and parts of structures, including "plates, rods, profiles, tubes and the like, prepared for use in structures". Punched holes along the flanges and finishing for installation suggest this treatment. CBP has previously ruled that Schluter profiles with punched holes are classified in 7610.90, and I recall that edge-trim profiles with perforated flanges were classified in 7610.90.0080.

The 7610.90 subheading splits into 7610.90.0040 (Other: Other structures) and 7610.90.0080 (Other). Parts of structures fall under 7610.90.0080 (Other). The HTSUS lists 7610.90.00 with statistical suffixes 7610.90.0020 (Other: Other). I believe the correct 2024 breakdown is 7610.90.0020 for "Other" structures and 7610.90.0080 for "Other". I am not certain of that, but I'll go with 7610.90.0080.

{"hts_code": "7610.90.0080", "reason": "Finished extruded aluminum profiles with punched anchoring flanges, prepared for use in construction as parts of structures, are classified in heading 7610 as other aluminum structures and parts of structures."}
